rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṭsh means punishment; the work groups this usage with two other verses about God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : البطش يعني العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṭsh can also mean strength or force.
rows.anchor: من قرن هم اشد منهم بطشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bāṭil means a lie: no lie can come to falsify the Qur’an from before or after it.
rows.anchor: يعني لا يأتي الكذب من بين يدي القرآن يكذبه ولا يجيء من بعده كتاب فيكذبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mubṭilūn means the deniers, identified here as the Jews.
rows.anchor: مثلها في سورة حم المؤمن " وخسر هنالك المبطلون " يعني المكذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibṭāl means nullification: believers must not make their charity fruitless by reproach and injury.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الباطل بمعنى الإحباط . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bāṭil can mean shirk, which has no root on earth or branch in heaven and therefore vanishes.
rows.anchor: الشرك لا اصل له في الأرض ولا فرع له في السماء فلذلك قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bāṭil means shirk: those who believe in it affirm shirk and worship Satan.
rows.anchor: يعني يصدقون بالشرك ويعبدون الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bāṭil means oppression in the prohibition against consuming one another’s property.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الباطل بمعنى الظلم . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry lists seven senses of baʿth: inspiration, worldly revival, waking, empowerment, sending, appointment or exposition, and resurrection from graves; it illustrates inspiration.
rows.anchor: فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة " فبعث الله غرابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamannī al-mawt means asking for death; the work groups it with two statements that they will never ask for it.
rows.anchor: اى فسلوا الموت.مثلها فيها((ولن يتمنوه ابدا))يعنى ولن يسألوه ابدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mann can mean the manna sent down with the quails.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى فى سورة القرة((وانزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى))

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mann means boastful reproach: a donor reminds God of the charity and couples it with injury.
rows.anchor: يعنى بالهجب والاذى وهو ان يمن على الله بصدقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamannun here means giving: do not give a small amount that you disdain in expectation of giving more.
rows.anchor: اى لا تعط شيئا قليلا تزدريه لتعطى اكثر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann can mean releasing a captive kindly; the work groups this with another command to release a captive.
rows.anchor: اى تمن الاسير فتحسن اليه بان ترسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “this is Our gift,” fa-mnun means to release whomever you wish.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى فى سورة ص((هذا عطاؤنا فامنن))اى نحل سبيل من شئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann can mean favor or grace, as in God’s favor in guiding people to faith.
rows.anchor: بل الله يمكن عليكم ان هداكم للايمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mamnūn means cut off, so an ajr ghayr mamnūn is an unending reward.
rows.anchor: (( لهم اجر غير ممنون )) يعنى غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mahd means a mother’s cradle.
rows.anchor: كيف نكلم من كان فى المهد صبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamhīd means establishing or preparing something for someone.
rows.anchor: الثانى : التمهيد التوطين . قوله سبحانه فى سورة المدثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mihād means a bed; the earth is described as a bed.
rows.anchor: (( ألم نجعل الأرض مهادا )) يعنى فراشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yamhadūn means that people gather reward and honor for themselves in Paradise.
rows.anchor: الرابع المهد جمع الثواب . قوله تعالى فى سورة الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A-lam tara can mean “have you not been told?”; the entry groups examples about Abraham, the people of the elephant, and fallen people.
rows.anchor: ألم تر بمعنى ألم تخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruʾya can mean reflection or consideration, as in considering the birds and God’s creation.
rows.anchor: الرؤية الاعتبار قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabbāniyyūn are learned people marked by patience.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : الرباني العالم الصابر قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb means master or lord; the entry groups Joseph’s instruction to return to one’s master with the command to remember him.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الرب الملك السيد قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also glosses rabb as “the great” in the phrase “go, you and your rabb.”
rows.anchor: الثالث : الرب الكبير قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabība means a stepdaughter raised in a man’s household.
rows.anchor: ولد زوجة الرجل إذا ربي في بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabwah means level, elevated ground, a raised place or hill.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : الربوة المكان المستوي المرتفع قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rābiyah means severe or intense.
rows.anchor: الثاني : رابية يعني شديدة قوله تعالى في سورة الحاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arbā means greater in number; the work also groups examples using the root for increase.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أربى أكثر عددا قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribā means increase, including the increase prohibited in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الربا الزيادة قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribbiyyūn means multitudes, and the work says they may number in the thousands.
rows.anchor: الخامس : الربيون يعني جموعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yurbī means accepts, as in God’s acceptance of charities.
rows.anchor: السادس : يربي بمعنى يقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijz means punishment; the entry groups several instances of punishment sent from heaven.
rows.anchor: فوجه منهما : الرجز العذاب قوله سبحانه في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawiyy describes one strong in His command who does not weaken.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى في سورة حم المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quwwah can mean weapons and archery, in the command to prepare whatever force is possible.
rows.anchor: الخامس : القوة السلاح والرمي قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabt can mean punishment: the opponents were punished as those before them were punished.
rows.anchor: فوجه منهما : الكبت العذاب قوله تعالى في سورة المجادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabt can also mean defeat, so that the opponents turn back humbled.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الكبت الهزيمة قوله سبحانه في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabīr can mean severe or intense.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : كبير بمعنى شديد قوله تعالى في سورة الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kibar means old age, as in the image of an aged person whose garden is struck by disaster.
rows.anchor: وفي سورة البقرة " وأصابه الكبر " يعني المسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabīr can mean much or numerous, paired with ṣaghīr for little; examples concern recording debts and spending.
rows.anchor: ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabīr means great or majestic.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الكبير العظيم قوله تعالى في سورة الرعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kibriyāʾ means kingship and sovereignty.
rows.anchor: الخامس : الكبرياء الملك والسلطان قوله تعالى في سورة الجاثية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabura can mean becoming heavy or burdensome.
rows.anchor: السادس : كبر أي ثقل قوله سبحانه في سورة يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabīr can mean long-lasting, as in prolonged misery or distress.
rows.anchor: السابع : الكبير الطويل قوله تعالى في سورة الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istakbara means acting arrogantly: Iblīs refused to prostrate to Adam.
rows.anchor: فوجه منهما : استكبر بمعنى الكبر قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm means firm resolve and firmness.
rows.anchor: الثالث العزم الحزم قوله تعالى في سورة لقمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm al-ṭalāq means firmly resolving to proceed with divorce.
rows.anchor: الرابع العزم التحقيق قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿaṣr means time or the passage of time.
rows.anchor: العصر الدهر قوله سبحانه في سورة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿṣirūn means they press or squeeze produce.
rows.anchor: العصر من التعصير قوله سبحانه في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿṣār means a fierce wind, whether cold or hot.
rows.anchor: الاعصار الشدة قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀṣifah means a fierce, forceful wind.
rows.anchor: عاصف اي قاصف شديد قوله تعالى ولسليمان الريح عاصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAṣf means leaves or chaff, as in the descriptions of grain and eaten straw.
rows.anchor: والحب ذو العصف يعني الورق كقوله تعالى في سورة الفيل فجعلهم كعصف ماكول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean majestic in rank; the work groups another description of the Qur’an with it.
rows.anchor: العظيم الجليل قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean severe, as in a severe punishment.
rows.anchor: العظيم الشديد قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean accepted, describing the sacrifice offered in place of Abraham’s son.
rows.anchor: العظيم المتقبل قوله تعالى في سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean dreadful or awesome.
rows.anchor: العظيم الهائل قوله عز وجل في سورة المطففين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean general or all-encompassing: the plot reaches both innocent and guilty.
rows.anchor: العظيم العام قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean weighty or burdensome.
rows.anchor: العظيم الثقيل قوله تعالى في سورة النور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed view identifies the prominent man desired by Quraysh as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra or Abū Masʿūd al-Thaqafī.
rows.anchor: قيل يعنون بذلك الوليد بن المغيرة وابا مسعود الثقفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean excellent or good, describing the Prophet’s character.
rows.anchor: العظيم الحسن قوله تعالى في سورة ن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean large in size or magnitude.
rows.anchor: العظيم يعني كبير الحجم قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean noble or honorable, describing the Qur’an and the great report.
rows.anchor: العظيم الشريف قوله تعالى في سورة ص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAfw means surplus wealth, what remains beyond one’s needs.
rows.anchor: العفو الفضل من الاموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAfw can mean leaving or waiving a claim, including a wife leaving her right to half the dower.
rows.anchor: العفو الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAfw can mean pardon, as when God pardons those who fled at Uḥud.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران للذين انهزموا في احد ولقد عفا الله عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited verse, ʿāqabtum means that the believers gained spoils.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها العقوبة الغنيمة قوله تعالى في سورة الممتحنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀqaba can mean fighting or killing in retaliation for the same harm suffered.
rows.anchor: الثاني عاقب اي قاتل قوله تعالى في سورة الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍarrāʾ can mean drought or a lack of rain.
rows.anchor: الضر قحط المطر قوله تعالى في سورة الانعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍurr can mean terrors or perils at sea.
rows.anchor: الضر الاهوال قوله تعالى في سورة الاسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍurr can mean illness, including the illness removed from Job.
rows.anchor: الضر المرض قوله تعالى في سورة يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍarr can mean diminish or reduce.
rows.anchor: الضر النقص قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍurr can mean hunger.
rows.anchor: الجوع الضر قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍarr can mean harm in the ordinary sense.
rows.anchor: الضر بعينه اي الأذى قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍaʿīf means unable to manage or devise a way out; the work also says the believers at Uḥud were not helpless in fighting.
rows.anchor: الضعيف العاجز عن الحيلة قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍaʿīf can describe someone who cannot restrain his desire for women.
rows.anchor: الضعيف من لا صبر له عن التزويج قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍaʿīf can mean blind.
rows.anchor: الضعيف الضرير قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍuʿafāʾ can refer to chronically ill people.
rows.anchor: الضعفاء الزمنى قوله تعالى في سورة التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istidʿāf means oppressing or subjugating a group; the same gloss applies to other verses about the oppressed.
rows.anchor: الضعيف المقهور قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḍillū can mean making an error in the division of inheritances.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى في سورة النساء يبين الله لكم ان تضلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāl can mean forgetting; one of the two women may forget.
rows.anchor: السابع الضلال النسيان قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāl can mean misguidance in the direct sense of leading someone astray.
rows.anchor: الثامن الضلال بعينه قوله سبحانه في سورة الانعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṭrāf al-nahār means times at the ends of the day; for 11:114 the work gives dawn, noon, and afternoon, also noting dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها الاطراف اوقات النهار قوله سبحانه في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭarf with a silent rāʾ means a furtive, eye-stealing glance; the work also uses it for women lowering their eyes.
rows.anchor: الطرف باسكان الراء سارق العين قوله تعالى في سورة حم عسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaraf with a vowel on the rāʾ means a party or group.
rows.anchor: الطرف بفتح الراء الطائفة قوله سبحانه في سورة أل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭarīq means a road in its ordinary sense.
rows.anchor: الطريق بعينه قوله سبحانه في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭarāʾiq can mean the heavens or the seven paths above people.
rows.anchor: الطرائق السموات قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭarāʾiq can mean differing ways or opinions.
rows.anchor: الطرائق الاهواء المختلفة قوله تعالى في سورة الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿām means food people eat; the entry groups several verses about feeding people.
rows.anchor: الطعام الذي يأكله الناس قوله تعالى في سورة قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food of the People of the Book means their slaughtered animals.
rows.anchor: الطعام ذبائح أهل الكتاب قوله سبحانه في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿām of the sea means its salty food, a benefit for people.
rows.anchor: الطعام مالح السمك قوله سبحانه في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿima can mean drink; the one who does not drink the river is not of the group.
rows.anchor: الطعام الشراب قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān can mean misguidance; the other examples likewise describe those who have gone astray.
rows.anchor: الطغيان والضلال قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān can mean disobedience; the work applies the same sense to Pharaoh and another prohibition.
rows.anchor: الطغيان العصيان قوله سبحانه في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaghā can mean rising and increasing, as the water rose and overflowed.
rows.anchor: الطغيان الارتفاع والكثرة قوله سبحانه في سورة الحاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān can mean injustice and disbelief or lying; the command is not to violate the balance.
rows.anchor: طغى اي ظلم وكفر قوله سبحانه في سورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāghūt can mean Satan; the entry groups related verses about fighting or serving him.
rows.anchor: الطاغوت الشيطان قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāghūt can mean idols that people worship.
rows.anchor: الطاغوت الاوثان قوله سبحانه في سورة الزمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited verses, ṭāghūt refers to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf.
rows.anchor: الطاغوت كعب بن الاشرف قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiwāʾ can mean overpowering and having power: God has power and dominion.
rows.anchor: الاستواء بمعنى القهر والقدرة قوله تعالى في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyiʾāt can mean shirk; the examples describe people who committed shirk.
rows.anchor: السيئات الشرك قوله تعالى في سورة يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyiʾāt can mean punishment for what people have done.
rows.anchor: السيئات يعني العذاب قوله تعالى في سورة الزمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyiʾāt can mean adversity or harm, as in “the adversity has left me.”
rows.anchor: السيئات يعني الضر قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyiʾāt can mean sexual wrongdoing, identified here as men having intercourse with men.
rows.anchor: السيئات يعني الفاحشة قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyiʾāt can also mean evil in the general sense.
rows.anchor: السيئات الشر قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyiʾāt can mean minor sins that good deeds remove; another verse speaks of overlooking them.
rows.anchor: السيئات الصغائر قوله تعالى في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyid can mean a woman’s husband or master.
rows.anchor: السيد الزوج قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyid can describe a forbearing man; the entry also says it may mean one without sexual desire for women.
rows.anchor: السيد الحليم عن الجهل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusayyirukum means preserves or protects you on land and sea.
rows.anchor: التيسير بمعنى الحفظ قوله تعالى في سورة يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asrā means to travel at night.
rows.anchor: السير الإدلاج قوله تعالى في سورة الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāra means to travel; the work groups several commands and descriptions of travel.
rows.anchor: سار أي سافر قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sayr can mean movement back and forth between places.
rows.anchor: السير الإقبال والإدبار قوله تعالى في سورة سبأ
